html:
Gedi is a ruined Swahili town in the forest near Malindi on the Kenyan coast, lived in from about the 12th century and abandoned in the 17th.

Its coral stone houses, palace, great mosque and pillar tombs lie within town walls. Finds include Chinese porcelain, Indian beads and Venetian glass, showing its links to the Indian Ocean trade, though it is not named in any known written record.

The town may have been left after Oromo raids, the fall of the water table, or attacks by Portuguese and others. It is one of the best preserved of the Swahili towns, with Lamu to the north.
sum: Gedi is a ruined Swahili town in the forest near Malindi on the Kenyan coast, lived in from about the 12th century and abandoned in the 17th.
